source_review.notes: Checked all ten final NASA and GAO references on 2026-08-31. Nine URLs returned HTTP 200 directly. GAO-20-151 was retrievable through the official GAO indexed product record, while its official page rejected the command-line client with HTTP 403; no stronger access claim is made. Reviewed active NASA-STD-8729.1A, NASA RCM guidance and facilities requirements, NASA glossary/lessons/Phase E/CM/V&V guidance, and GAO reliability practices. Facility, spaceflight, acquisition, and institutional scopes are explicit and require tailoring.

evidence: Reviewed restoration thread from failure through detection, isolation, safeing/support, access, repair, verification, and return to service.
Reviewed simple renewal operational-availability expression with consistent mean-up and mean-down boundaries.
Reviewed maintenance-event intervals and explicit dependence of MTTR/MDT inclusion on governing definitions.
Reviewed detection and isolation coverage denominators and the need to define failure population, isolation depth, and ambiguity.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes active work, delays, restoration evidence, capability state, and statistical boundary rather than treating repair time as universal downtime.

evidence: Executed maintainability-restoration-fixture under python3 with exact output in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-088/report.json.
Recomputed six active intervals as 70 minutes and MDT with logistics as 110 minutes.
Recomputed fixture availability 990/(990+110)=0.900 and confirmed replace is the longest declared active step.
Recomputed Exercise 2 MDT as 150 minutes and availability 1440/1590 approximately 90.57 percent.
Recomputed Exercise 3 detection coverage 95 percent, single-module isolation 72 percent overall or approximately 75.79 percent among detections, and healthy-trial false-alarm fraction 9 percent.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Deterministic and aggregate arithmetic omits distributions, confidence, censoring, dependence, partial capability, failure mix, observation bias, and mission demand.

evidence: Confirmed short active replacement time does not entail short total downtime or adequate support.
Confirmed BIT indication does not entail isolated root cause or correct module replacement.
Confirmed preventive or predictive action does not entail beneficial maintenance without mechanism, actionable lead time, and intervention evidence.
Confirmed spare quantity does not entail readiness without compatibility, provenance, location, condition, access, and repair flow.
Confirmed completed work order, cleared alarm, or online service does not entail authorized restoration.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter consistently limits inference from averages, diagnostic codes, predictions, inventory, vendor support, automation, and availability ratios.

evidence: Challenged failure recognition and timing boundaries, long-tail logistics, parallel work, partial capability, deferred work, censored events, site/variant mix, and misleading availability improvement.

Challenged intermittent/combined/common-cause faults, sensor/BIT failure, ambiguity, no-fault-found, false removals, maintenance-induced damage, intrusive schedules, and inadequate prediction lead time.
Challenged access with protective equipment, posture/force/visibility, contamination/energy, fatigue/language, degraded communications, offline remote support, credentials, and emergency maintenance.

Challenged mismatched spare firmware/calibration/keys, counterfeit/provenance, repair yield/turnaround, surge, tool/facility/calibration failure, supplier/rights/skill obsolescence, software/data corruption, and recovery configuration.
Reviewed all ten examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limitations, effectivity, safety/security, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real support decisions require applicable system/domain, reliability/maintainability, human factors, safety/security, supply/logistics, software/data/platform, facilities/tools, supplier/quality, V&V, operations, records, and technical-authority expertise.

evidence: Confirmed maintenance/support concepts derive from mission, environment, horizon, criticality, availability, workforce, access, logistics, hazards/threats, and retirement.
Confirmed requirements specify event boundaries, conditions, distributions/percentiles, confidence, exclusions, and effectivity.
Confirmed design integrates containment, safeing, access, modularity, diagnostics, handling, digital recovery, procedures, support resources, verification, and return authority.
Confirmed maintenance policy follows function/failure consequence and includes reactive, preventive, condition-based, failure-finding, run-to-failure, and redesign choices.
Confirmed work records bind fault, action, installed/removed identity, software/data, tools/calibration, deviations, evidence, actual configuration, and approval.
Confirmed closure verifies restoration and regression, reconciles effectivity, replenishes support, learns from outcomes, and handles evolution/retirement.
invariant_checking.notes: No MTTR average, accessible CAD model, BIT code, prediction score, spare count, vendor contract, automated restart, work-order closure, or availability dashboard is treated as sufficient alone.

proof_review.notes: No formal proof or theorem requires proof review; restoration and renewal availability are bounded engineering models.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is labeled or presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Executable output is labeled declared_deterministic_intervals_only.

Fixture limitations disclaim distributions, censoring, parallel work, preventive downtime, partial capability, multiple failures, logistics variation, safety/security, configuration, quality, and observation bias.
Examples and exercises are synthetic teaching cases, not actual maintenance demonstrations, reliability studies, diagnostic qualifications, return-to-service approvals, or support authorizations.
Official sources are attributed without claiming NASA or GAO review, approval, or endorsement of this chapter.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic arithmetic, source-backed guidance, internal review, maintenance demonstration, operational evidence, and technical return authority remain distinct.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked maintainability/support distinctions, maintenance concepts and levels, measurement boundaries, allocation, containment/degradation, replaceable units, physical/digital access, diagnosis, maintenance policy, support enterprise, supply/repair, technical data, configuration, restoration evidence, learning, measures, evolution, and retirement.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked physical and software/platform maintenance, RCM choices, BIT/condition monitoring, human access, spares/repair, tools/calibration/facilities, remote/vendor support, work records, safety/security, fleet/site effectivity, return to service, operational metrics, obsolescence, and last repairs.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from mission context and maintenance concept through design, diagnosis, policy, support, work control, restoration, feedback, and retirement. Ten examples and five complete solutions cover physical access, false isolation, data recovery, preventive risk, spare compatibility, prognostics, human factors, emergency patching, metric gaming, and tool obsolescence.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external NASA/GAO expert, reliability/maintainability engineer, maintenance planner/technician, human-factors specialist, safety/security authority, supply/logistics/quality manager, software/data/platform owner, facilities/tool/calibration specialist, supplier/vendor, V&V authority, operator/customer, records/environmental authority, auditor, or other external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
